reason: The cited evidence (E1) describes Mg-Ti-Zn alloys processed by ball milling and spark plasma sintering, but it reports the formation of intermetallic phases in the as-sintered state, not a metastable single-phase solid solution. It provides no data on annealing-driven precipitation, oxide film modulation by precipitates, or correlations between precipitate evolution and corrosion/oxidation resistance. Thus, none of the key premises are supported by the cited passage.
premises: Mg-containing lightweight HEA can be processed into a metastable, single-phase, supersaturated solid solution
Annealing at ~450 °C causes diffusion-controlled nucleation and growth of intermetallic precipitates
Intermetallic precipitates alter local chemistry at grain boundaries and within the matrix
Precipitate-induced chemical changes modulate protective oxide film formation and stability
Corrosion and oxidation resistance correlate with intermetallic precipitate evolution
